```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h1Data$Religion_type <- factor(h1Data$Religion_type,
                           levels = c("Christianity", "Islam", 
                                      "Hinduism", "Buddhism", "Other", "Judaism", "None"))
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
```

## H1: Religious affiliation & time spent living in country of birth

We predict religious affiliation will predict time spent living in country of birth.

### Variables & descriptive statistics

- **Religious affiliation ('Religion_type'):** A categorical variable with seven groups: Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Other, Judaism, & None.
- **Time Spent living in country of birth ('Country_live_time'):** A continuous variable measuring the number of years respondents have lived in their country of birth. Valid responses range from 1-80.


```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$Religion_type)

# Summarize attractiveness points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$Country_live_time, h1Data$Religion_type, summary)
                                                   #can do table or other functions, not just summary
```

### Graph

@fig-religion shows the distribution of years spent living in country of birth by religious affiliation.
The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes
the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-religion
#| fig-cap: "Time spent living in country of birth by religious affiliation."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Religion_type, y = Country_live_time, fill = Religion_type)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Religious affiliation", y = "Years spent living in country of birth") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


## H2. Sociosexuality & relationship duration

We predict casual sexual experiences & preferences will predict relationship duration.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Sociosexuality composite ('soiComposite'):** The mean of available responses to 'soi_behave', 'soi_attitude', & 'soi_desire'. Each item ranges from 1 to 9, with higher scores indicating more unrestricted sociosexuality. 
- **Relationship duration ('relationship_length'):** A variable representing the length of respondendts' current relationships. Responses range from 1 to 80, with higer values indicating longer relationship duration.

This dataset includes respondents who were dating, in a committed
relationship, or married.


```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("soiComposite", "Relationship_length")])
```

### Graph

@fig-relationship shows the relationship sociosexuality relationship 
duration Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to
see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear
trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-relationship
#| fig-cap: "Sociosexuality composite scores and relationship duration."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = soiComposite, y = Relationship_length)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04, alpha = .04, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Sociosexuality composite score (1–9)",
       y = "Relationship duration (1–80)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$soiComposite, h2Data$Relationship_length, use = "complete.obs")
#r is value, 2 is the decimal spot to round to
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative
association. Respondents with higher sociosexuality composite scores tended to report shorter relationship duration
